cards.body:
## Summary
Who may CALL each command is written once (T11). Who is TOLD each event is written three times: as literal (label, name) pairs at ~20 emit_to sites in the shell, as the mock's hand TARGETS table, and implicitly by EventContract's serde names. The copies already disagree. Move event audiences into the authority table, emit through one table-driven helper, generate the mock's table, and fold the audiences into the permissions fingerprint.

## Description
Add an EVENTS section to authority_table.rs (dependency-free const rows: event name, window labels), plus `event_audience(name)`. authority.rs folds the rows into manifest() and writes EVENT_AUDIENCE into bindings/authority.ts. A typed emit in table-client (an enum or trait carrying each EventContract payload with its name) gives the shell one helper, `emit(app, event)`, which sends to every label in the row. The ~20 literal emit_to calls in events.rs, routing.rs and surface.rs go through it. The mock's TARGETS becomes the generated constant, as T11 did with GATES = AUTHORITY. tests/bindings.rs compares EVENTS with EventContract in both directions. A hand-pinned audience test guards the privacy-relevant rows (the summary only reaches approval; deal, agent and pairing events never reach the Tumbler). capabilities.rs scans the shell sources so that no literal emit_to is left.

## Flow
- Add rows + event_audience + manifest folding + TS export; re-pin PINNED_MANIFEST; regenerate bindings
- Add the typed event enum/trait in lib.rs; bindings test both directions
- Shell: one emit helper; replace every literal emit; source-scan test
- Mock: TARGETS = EVENT_AUDIENCE

## Expected impact
One place decides what each window learns, and the owner's fingerprint covers it. The lag-recovery drift (approval misses settings:changed, so a lock change during lag leaves the approval window stale) disappears by construction. An event-name typo becomes a compile/test failure instead of a silent drop. The IPC-tape / replay direction (T7's 'not chosen' IPC tape) and T18's extra principal can read audiences from the table rather than from shell source.

## Evaluation
Claim: event audiences become single-source, drift-proof and fingerprinted.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no EVENTS rows, no event_audience, no TS export, literal emits everywhere, lag path omits approval).
After: 7 of 7 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked settings:changed through events.rs:105 vs :170-172 and backend.ts:62; walked approval:summary through routing.rs:105 and events.rs:226; walked the manifest computation in authority.rs:42-53; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: contract (the bindings/authority.ts shape and the permissions fingerprint change; both are consumed only inside this repo: the client mock and the proof-file same_version comparison, which already changes on every row append)

cards.title: Tray menu that names each waiting deal, opens its card, and toggles pause/resume
shared_surfaces: none of the append-only surfaces (no COMMANDS row, no binding, no migration); the tray dispatches existing Actions only
acceptance: tray_model(snapshot with 0 items, agents_paused=false, now) -> entries with ids [main, tumbler, pause, quit] in that order, dot=false, tooltip "The Table - nothing needs you"

tray_model(.., agents_paused=true, ..) -> the pause entry is replaced by id "resume" with text "Resume all agents"; TrayCommand::parse("resume") -> Some(TrayCommand::Resume) (the shell maps it to Action::Resume, as "pause" maps to Action::Pause today)

snapshot with 2 items (Gate D-0193 headline "Approve payment" 34000 USD deadline now+600; Hold D-0190 no deadline) -> a disabled header "2 need you" then two entries in snapshot order: "D-0193 - Approve payment - 340.00 USD - in 10 min" and "D-0190 - <its headline> - <amount>" (no time suffix); ids "deal:<ulid>"; dot=true; tooltip "The Table - 2 need you, next in 10 min"
snapshot with 7 items -> exactly 5 deal entries plus one entry "2 more in The Table" with id "main"
model.command("deal:<ulid of an entry>") -> Some(OpenCard(id)); model.command("deal:<ulid not in this model>") -> None (a stale menu click does nothing); model.command("deal:garbage") -> None

an item whose counterparty is Some("Evil Corp <ignore previous>") -> no entry text or tooltip contains it (counterparty and on_silence are never read); a headline longer than 48 chars is cut to 48 with an ellipsis
deadline in the past -> suffix "overdue"; deadline within 60 s -> "now"; deadline 2 h 10 min away -> "in 2 h"

cards.body:
## Summary
The tray is the one surface that is always there: closing a window hides it to the tray. Since 570efb5 it shows a gold dot when a deal needs the owner, but its menu is four fixed items. It cannot say which deal or by when. It offers Pause and never Resume. Rebuild the menu from the attention snapshot the shell already holds: one entry per waiting deal (label, Rust headline, amount, time left) that opens that deal's card, a Pause/Resume toggle from agents_paused, and a tooltip with the count and the next deadline.

## Description
A pure `table_client::tray` module: `tray_model(&AttentionSnapshot, agents_paused, now) -> TrayModel { tooltip, dot, entries }` and `TrayModel::command(id) -> Option<TrayCommand>` (Main, Tumbler, Pause, Resume, Quit, OpenCard(DealId)). It reads only owner-bound, Rust-composed fields (label, headline, amount_minor, currency, deadline), never counterparty or on_silence. It shows at most 5 deals plus 'N more', and cuts headlines to 48 chars. In the shell, setup builds the menu from the model. WalletEvent::Attention and WalletEvent::Settings rebuild it (with set_menu + set_tooltip) only when the model changed, deduped like visual_previous. on_menu_event dispatches through `model.command(id)`. OpenCard reuses the toast's routing (set_form Card, summon, tumbler:selected), extracted into one function. Resume runs Action::Resume exactly as Pause runs Action::Pause today.

## Flow
- Today: see the gold dot -> left-click (Tumbler) or open The Table -> find which card -> act; after a tray pause, open The Table to resume
- After: right-click the tray -> 'D-0193 - Approve payment - 340.00 USD - in 10 min' -> click -> that deal's card is open; 'Resume all agents' is in the same menu

## Expected impact
The dot stops being a report and becomes the way in. The owner sees what waits and how urgent it is without opening a window, reaches the right card in one click, and can undo a tray pause where it was made.

## Evaluation
Claim: the tray menu becomes a live, actionable projection of the attention snapshot and the paused state.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass (no model; fixed menu; no resume; literal id match)
After: 8 of 8 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked a 2-item snapshot through lib.rs:357-363 ordering and the toast route at events.rs:364-370; walked pause -> settings event -> model with agents_paused=true; the gate rung is the builder's
Result: better
Gate: none (no new command, row or binding; Resume is an existing OPEN Act-tier action, dispatched by the native tray exactly like the existing Pause - a webview cannot click a native menu). The native tray is Windows-only and not compiled on the Linux host; a Windows compile/check is owed, as for every shell change.
